newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv says sales rose three pct H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv says sales rose three pct H1 1997.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. car safety equipment maker Autoliv Inc said on Monday sales rose three percent in the first half of 1997, with airbag sales up four percent and seatbelt sales rising one percent.
Autoliv Inc., formed on May 1 through a merger of Sweden's Autoliv AB and U.S. Morton International's car safety division ASP, posted six-month sales of $1.68 billion.
The company said it would pay a dividend of $0.11 per share on September 4.

Autoliv posted a somewhat higher than expected profit after financial items of $177 million for the first six months of the year, up from $161 million in the corresponding year-earlier period. Analysts had targeted $169 million.
But its share came off day-highs of 302 crowns on the news and was changing hands at 296.5 crowns on the Stockholm Stock Exchange at 1540 GMT, up 3.5 crowns from its Friday close.
"Speculation drove the share higher ahead of the report," a trader said. "But the report was slightly better than expected, or roughly in line with expectations."
Earnings per share rose to $1.01 in the first half from $0.90 and to $0.47 in the second quarter from $0.42.
Second quarter sales rose three percent to $849 but excluding the effect of the stronger dollar they rose 10 percent, the company said.
The market was mixed, the company said.
"Prices have continued to fall. The manufacturing of light vehicles in the U.S. and Europe, Autoliv's most important markets, is expected to have increased by two percent," the company said.
The profit improvement stemmed largely from increased sales and continued productivity improvements, the company said.
